note: Clean row: verified address and a permitted country. The control every other case is compared against.
Second clean row so a campaign-scoped query returns more than one account.
Mixed-case spelling of the row below. Normalization must collapse the two or a suppression recorded against one would not stop a send to the other.
Lowercase spelling of the row above. The same mailbox once normalized.
Same account domain and same person name as the row below but a different address: dedup must decide on identity and not on the address alone.
The www prefix and mixed case must normalize to the same account as the row above.
Outside the default allowed countries. Hard eligibility must refuse it while the pilot stays domestic.
Intended target of a suppression record. Suppression must outrank an otherwise eligible verified contact.
No reachable address at all. Import must accept the contact and eligibility must refuse the send rather than inventing one.
Syntactically valid and known undeliverable. Policy requires a verified address so this must never reach a send.
Never checked rather than known bad. Unverified is not a soft yes and must be refused the same way.
One account plausible for both campaigns. Campaign membership is per candidate so this must become two candidates and never one shared judgement.
A second contact at the same both-campaign account so account-level and contact-level dedup can be told apart.
Country unknown at import. Unknown geography must be refused rather than assumed domestic.
Reachable by something that is not email. An email-only policy must not silently treat this as a sendable address.
